claims.statement: INIT at $1000 JMPs to $10F1; PLAY at $1003 JMPs to $1126.
claims.howToVerify: Check entry JMP operands and executed control-flow edges.

claims.statement: STA $10F6 at $10F1 writes the immediate operand of ADC at $10F5; $10F6 is executable code storage, not a stand-alone source state byte. For A=0, it writes the existing value $00.
claims.howToVerify: Verify $10F5=[69 00] and the executed absolute store at $10F1; instrument writes including unchanged-value writes.

claims.statement: For subtune-selector A values 0,1,2, $10F4 ASL A followed by $10F5 ADC #(original A) computes 3*A (0,3,6) and $10F7 stores that byte at $1129. This is source-code arithmetic; only A=0 was traced.
claims.howToVerify: Run INIT(A=0), INIT(A=1), INIT(A=2) on independent resets; observe $1129=0,3,6 and carry/flags.

claims.statement: Byte $1129 is the immediate operand of LDY #$FF at $1128 in the PLAY routine; INIT changes it to $00 for the observed subtune.
claims.howToVerify: Inspect initial bytes [A0 FF], operand write from $10F7, and first runtime LDY variant [A0 00].

claims.statement: The first PLAY executes LDY #$00; BMI at $112A is NOT taken and execution enters $112C, whereas on the next 299 observed PLAY calls LDY #$FF makes BMI taken to $1161.
claims.howToVerify: Check actual executed LDY variants and both BMI edge counts for the 300-frame trace.

claims.statement: At $113E, the one-time initialization path executes STX $1129, restoring the LDY immediate operand to $FF and causing later PLAY calls to skip that path.
claims.howToVerify: Verify X=$FF after the 42-iteration DEX/BPL clear loop, the recorded $1129 operand patch $00->$FF, and later LDY #$FF variants.

claims.statement: The one-time setup selects voice-table offsets X=0,7,14 on three linked initialization paths; the exact semantic identities of the referenced tables still require separate evidence.
claims.howToVerify: Trace the paths through $1142/$1145/$1147/$114A and memory effects downstream of $114C.

claims.statement: The source uses instruction-operand patching as a deferred one-time initialization mechanism; generated PAY code can preserve its behaviour with a dedicated absolute-RAM pending-init flag and subtune-derived index instead.
claims.howToVerify: Compare reconstructed first and subsequent PLAY state changes for all subtunes against source traces.

Run the one-time voice-table and channel-state setup using subtune index (0,3,6); then set first_play_pending=false. Source takes BMI not-taken path $112C and patches $1129 back to $FF.
Execute regular per-tick player path corresponding to BMI taken at $112A->$1161. Further semantics delegated to other mechanisms.

soundTranslation.sourceIntent: Deferred subtune setup and first-PLAY initialization, implemented by source code-operand patches.
soundTranslation.AYStrategy: Replace source self-modification with explicit absolute-RAM selected-subtune index and first-tick-pending state; retain source state-transition order. No AY writes are implied by this mechanism alone.
soundTranslation.limitations: Table semantics, full 3-subtune coverage, and source clock cadence remain unverified. Do not generate a standalone song from this mechanism.

proposedTests.experiment: RESET source memory; INIT(A=0), INIT(A=1), INIT(A=2) separately, then inspect $10F6/$1129 before any PLAY.
proposedTests.expectedObservables: $10F6 is 0/1/2 and $1129 is 0/3/6, respectively; the byte at $10F5 remains opcode $69 and $1128 remains opcode $A0.

proposedTests.experiment: For each subtune, execute exactly first PLAY then second PLAY with operand writes (including same-value writes) and branch edges instrumented.
proposedTests.expectedObservables: First PLAY reads initial patched LDY value, takes BMI fall-through, and resets operand to $FF; second PLAY takes BMI $1161.

proposedTests.experiment: Trace source writes from first-PLAY setup, including accesses for X=0,7,14, for all three subtunes.
proposedTests.expectedObservables: Identify the selected three-table-entry ranges and their effects on subsequent voice state; explain whether the grouped indices 0..2,3..5,6..8 represent separate song setups.
